summary: Frontend-only verification of the WavyLayer overlay rebuild (dedicated absolute-space projected layer instead of drawing inside each note's rotated/perspective-scaled container). BOTH PRIMARY SCENARIOS PASS. (1) Wavy ribbon render + no crash: Home → browse-library-button → device-library-chip → song-card-neon-warmup → difficulty-normal-chip → play-generated-chart-button → 3-2-1 countdown → gameplay-screen visible for ~13s of play (six frames captured across the run). Wavy notes render as a SINGLE clean glowing ribbon that follows the highway lanes and converges toward the vanishing point (see gp_0.jpeg — a smooth curved ribbon from top-right descending toward the receptor, correctly perspective-projected; gp_1/gp_4 also show clean ribbons). NO sheared/rotated/warped blob, NO red screen, NO crash. pause-game-button → exit-game-button returns to /library cleanly. (2) Editor wave shape faithful: /editor → editor-open-library-button → device-library-chip → Voco Warmup → skipped tutorial → editor-record-button → horizontal sine drag across the board → editor-note-count went from '0 NOTES · CUSTOM CHART' to '1 NOTES · CUSTOM CHART' → save-chart-button → 'Chart saved ✓' toast appeared. The placed wavy note renders as a clean smooth ribbon that visibly matches the drag path (see ed2_04_after_drag.jpeg — the pink ribbon curves from bottom-left up to top-right along the exact drag trajectory). Regression sanity: normal tap notes (colored pills) and hold tail (right-side purple hold bar) render correctly during gameplay; navigation between screens is stable; pause/exit works. Results screen was verified end-to-end in iteration_8 (no results-related code changes this iteration). No new bugs found.

critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/app/game.tsx L45-82: New WavyNote / WavyLayer renders in ABSOLUTE highway space and projects each recorded (t, x) point via the same perspective the lanes use (persp = P_NEAR + (1-P_NEAR)*cp, x = cx + (p.x-0.5)*2*hw*persp, y = topY + span*cp). Ribbon = three stacked AnimatedPaths (glow halo + main + white core). This is what produces the clean lane-aligned ribbon seen in gp_0.jpeg and eliminates the previous shear from the per-note rotateZ/scale wrapper.

/app/frontend/app/game.tsx L83-85: WavyLayer only filters notes where n.type === 'wavy' and lives above NotesLayer inside a single StyleSheet.absoluteFill container — good separation from FallingNote's per-note transform.

/app/frontend/app/game.tsx L136-153: ActiveHoldBar early-returns null when isWavy, correctly suppressing the previous distorted draining bar so the falling ribbon + lit receptor guide the trace instead.
/app/frontend/app/editor.tsx L37-60: editor waveData uses contourPath in absolute board space too, so the placed wavy note matches what the finger drew (verified in ed2_04_after_drag.jpeg).

game.tsx = 518 lines, editor.tsx = 364 lines, chartEngine.ts = 176 lines — all under the 700-line splitting threshold. No DRY violation for smoothPath (duplicated intentionally in game.tsx and editor.tsx for their respective coordinate systems).

rca_of_issue: N/A — no bugs found. The wavy-note distortion the user was frustrated with is resolved: previously the wave path was drawn inside each note's rotateZ/scale/perspective wrapper (FallingNote), so the sine got sheared/rotated with the note container. The rebuild moves wavy rendering into a dedicated WavyLayer that lives in absolute highway space and projects each path point through the same perspective transform the lanes use. Result: the ribbon now traces the actual lane centers and follows the highway's vanishing point instead of appearing as a rotated distorted blob.
